title: Ishan Kishan Ruled Out of Wellington T20I Despite Recovering Well
excerpt: The BCCI says Kishan is recovering from a low-grade right adductor strain but has not regained match fitness for the October 27 third T20I.
body:
• Ishan Kishan is recovering well from a low-grade right adductor strain but is ruled out of the third T20I against New Zealand on October 27 in Wellington, the BCCI said.
  • Kishan sustained the injury in the first T20I and also missed the second match; Kumar Kushagra will continue with the team as cover.
  • Vaibhav Sooryavanshi took Kishan's place in the second T20I and scored 4 off 8 balls.
  • India lead the five-match series 2-0 and can seal it at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday.

India wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the third T20I against New Zealand despite recovering well from injury, the Board of Control for Cricket in India announced on Monday. Kishan is yet to regain match fitness after a low-grade right adductor strain sustained in the first match of the series, according to Cricbuzz.

The BCCI statement, quoted by both Cricbuzz and IANS, said: "He is yet to regain match fitness and is ruled out of the third T20I to be played on October 27, 2026 in Wellington. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring Ishan's progress."

"Ishan Kishan is recovering well from his low grade right adductor strain, which he sustained during the first T20I of the series against New Zealand. He is yet to regain match fitness and is ruled out of the third T20I to be played on October 27, 2026 in Wellington."

— BCCI

Second Match Missed, Cover Continues

Kishan missed the second match of the series as well. Kumar Kushagra, who had been drafted in as his replacement for the second T20I, will continue to keep his place in the side for the third match, set to be played at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday.

https://x.com/CricSubhayan/status/2114237402768105521

In Kishan's absence in the second T20I, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was handed an opportunity in the playing XI. The youngster managed just four runs off eight deliveries, IANS reported. The Wellington match offers him another opportunity to make an impression, with Kishan yet to recover.

India's Squad and the Series Picture

India currently lead the five-match series 2-0, Cricbuzz reported, and can seal the series in Wellington, with New Zealand eager to pull one back. IANS listed India's squad for the third T20I as: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wicketkeeper), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav and Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper).

Kishan had featured in a historic win for India in the series opener, when the team chased down its highest-ever total in men's T20I history, before the adductor strain ruled him out. An adductor strain is a groin-area muscle injury; the BCCI has described Kishan's as low grade, and its wording — recovering well, but not yet match fit — points to a precautionary absence rather than a setback.

What to Watch Next

No return date has been announced. The BCCI medical team is monitoring Kishan's progress, and his availability for the remaining two matches of the five-match series will depend on regaining match fitness. For now, India go into Tuesday's Wellington T20I with Sanju Samson and Kumar Kushagra as the wicketkeeping options, and a chance to close out the series without one of their most explosive top-order batters.
